openingPrayer.title: Steady My Heart
openingPrayer.body: Lord, before I read what this day holds, steady my heart in Your peace. The world carries grief and uncertainty, yet You remain unshaken, near to the brokenhearted and mighty to save. Give me eyes to see with compassion, a mind grounded in truth, and a spirit that trusts Your sovereignty over every headline. Where there is sorrow, let me grieve with hope; where there is good news, let me rejoice with gratitude. Keep my heart anchored in You alone, today and always. Amen.

articles.headline: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing after flash floods in Nepal and Tibet
articles.summary: Flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border have killed hundreds of people and left more than 1,000 missing, according to NPR. The floods swept away roads, bridges, and entire villages. BBC News reports that experts now fear a newly formed barrier lake, created by a recent landslide in the area, could trigger a second flood.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by NPR (multiple reports) and BBC News

articles.headline: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 and his son becomes King Haakon VIII
articles.summary: King Harald V of Norway has died at age 89, according to NPR, and his son has become King Haakon VIII. NPR notes Harald lived in exile in the United States as a child during the Nazi occupation of Norway and later married his school sweetheart rather than a European noblewoman. BBC News reports the transition comes at a turbulent time for Norway's monarchy, with Oslo's mayor postponing her own wedding out of respect.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by NPR and BBC News

verse.text: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble. Therefore we will not fear, though the earth give way and the mountains fall into the heart of the sea.
verse.reflection: For the families in Nepal still searching for loved ones amid the floodwaters, and for a nation mourning the loss of a king, this psalm offers a steady anchor: even when the ground beneath us gives way, God remains a refuge close at hand.

articles.headline: Judge rules Pentagon's actions against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'
articles.summary: A federal judge issued a written order stating the Pentagon acted illegally in punishing AI company Anthropic over its criticism of the Department of Defense's approach to AI use, according to NPR and BBC News. The government is expected to appeal the ruling. The dispute centers on tensions between the Trump administration and the AI startup over military use of artificial intelligence.

articles.headline: Jury deliberates in murder trial of Lindsay Clancy
articles.summary: A jury has begun deliberating in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, a Massachusetts woman accused of killing her three young children, according to BBC News and NPR. Prosecutors argued the killings were a calculated act, while the defense contended Clancy was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time. Closing statements from both sides were delivered before deliberations began.

verse.text: He has shown you, O mortal, what is good. And what does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.reflection: Today's headlines hold both a court weighing government overreach and a jury wrestling with a mother's unimaginable tragedy and mental illness. In both, we're reminded that true justice never stands apart from mercy — a balance only God can fully hold, and one we're called to seek even in our hardest judgments.

articles.headline: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 and his son becomes King Haakon VIII
articles.summary: Norway's King Harald V has died at the age of 89, according to NPR and BBC News. His son, now known as King Haakon VIII, has ascended to the throne, with BBC News noting the transition comes at a turbulent time for Norway's monarchy. Related ceremonies and events, including a planned Oslo wedding, have reportedly been postponed following the king's death.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by 3 outlets (NPR and two BBC News reports)

articles.headline: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America
articles.summary: President Trump has signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario as 'Lake America,' according to NPR and BBC News. BBC News reports that Canada has rejected the new name, since the lake straddles both countries, deepening tensions between the two nations. The dispute adds to ongoing friction in U.S.-Canada relations.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by 2 outlets (NPR and BBC News)

verse.text: He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings; he gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
verse.reflection: Today's news carries the weight of thrones changing hands and nations disputing even the names on their maps — reminders that human power is always shifting. In the midst of it, this verse invites us to trust that God's authority over history remains steady, even when ours feels uncertain.

articles.headline: Businesses are getting tariff refunds. Why aren't consumers getting their cut?
articles.summary: According to NPR, numerous American companies are receiving billions of dollars in tariff refunds following a Supreme Court ruling. NPR reports that many consumers who paid higher prices due to those tariffs may not see any of that money returned to them.

articles.headline: U.S. says pipelines will make Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Energy experts disagree
articles.summary: NPR reports that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed new oil pipelines will render the Strait of Hormuz irrelevant within two years. However, NPR notes that energy experts are skeptical this outcome is likely, given the strait's continued importance to global oil transport.

verse.text: A false balance is an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is his delight.
verse.reflection: When refunds flow easily to corporations but not to the everyday people who paid the price, it's worth remembering that God cares deeply about fairness in every transaction, big or small. May today's leaders and markets be shaped by honesty, not just efficiency.

articles.headline: $17B settlement between Meta, states also comes with new safeguards for teens
articles.summary: Meta has reached a $17 billion settlement with U.S. states over concerns about child safety on Facebook and Instagram, according to NPR. The agreement introduces new safeguards for teen users, and a former Meta researcher weighed in on whether the changes will be effective in practice. BBC News reports the settlement is also prompting scrutiny of other platforms, including TikTok and YouTube, as regulators consider broader reforms to protect young users online.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated across multiple NPR reports and BBC News.

articles.headline: Judge says Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'
articles.summary: A federal judge ruled that the Pentagon acted illegally when it took punitive action against AI company Anthropic after the company criticized the Department of Defense's approach to AI, NPR reports. The written order, issued Thursday night, described the government's measures as baseless. NPR notes the government is expected to challenge the ruling.

verse.text: Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed.
verse.reflection: Today's news touches both the protection of children online and a court standing up against unjust use of power—two reminders that justice and care for the vulnerable matter in every arena, even the digital one. May we trust that these small, hard-won steps toward accountability reflect a deeper call to defend those who cannot defend themselves.

articles.headline: UK salmonella cases nearing 500 as egg investigations continue
articles.summary: BBC News reports that a salmonella outbreak linked to imported eggs has sickened close to 500 people across the UK, according to health authorities. Investigators are continuing to examine additional clusters of illness as the outbreak grows.

articles.headline: FDA approves landmark pancreatic cancer drug that's shown to improve survival
articles.summary: NPR reports that U.S. health officials have approved a new pancreatic cancer drug shown to improve patient survival rates. The drug works by blocking a protein that fuels tumor growth in the majority of pancreatic cancer cases, according to the report.

verse.text: The Lord sustains him on his sickbed and restores him from his bed of illness.
verse.reflection: Whether it's an outbreak spreading fear through a community or a new drug offering fresh hope to cancer patients, healing remains a fragile and precious gift. May we hold both the sick and the scientists working to help them in our prayers today.

articles.headline: A melting glacier contributed to the deadly Nepal floods. We can expect more like this
articles.summary: According to NPR, scientists say a glacial collapse in the Himalayas triggered flash floods that killed and displaced people across Nepal and Tibet, with researchers warning that a warming climate will make such disasters more frequent. BBC News reports that more than 1,300 people remain missing, including dozens of Americans and Canadians, and survivors have described family members being swept away by the floodwaters. BBC's separate coverage confirms experts point to glacial collapse as the flood's trigger.
articles.trustNote: Corroborated by 2 outlets (NPR and BBC News, multiple articles)

articles.headline: NASA is about to launch a space telescope that could change how we see the universe
articles.summary: NPR reports that NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is scheduled to launch on August 30, with a mission to investigate major cosmic questions including the nature of dark energy and the behavior of supernovae. The telescope is expected to expand astronomers' ability to study large regions of the universe in detail.

verse.text: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you.
verse.reflection: As families in Nepal grieve loved ones swept away by floodwaters, this promise doesn't erase the sorrow but reminds us that God does not abandon us in the deep places. Even as we marvel at new telescopes unveiling the vastness of creation, may we hold close the truth that the same God who set the stars in place walks with the suffering here on earth.

articles.headline: ‘Our immigrants are invisible’: A pastor ministers to the frightened at immigration court
articles.summary: The Rev. Eduardo Fabian Arias, a Lutheran pastor in Manhattan, has spent years ministering to immigrants and now regularly accompanies them inside and around the Federal Plaza immigration court, according to RNS. His work has taken on new urgency as ICE conducts patrols near the courthouse, RNS reports.

articles.headline: The Museum of the Bible is offering a Christian nationalist vision of America’s past
articles.summary: According to RNS, the Museum of the Bible presents an interpretation of American history that seeks to unite people of faith around the idea that efforts to 're-establish' a Christian America are rooted in the nation's founding. The report frames this as part of a broader movement described as Christian nationalism.

verse.text: For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me.
verse.reflection: Pastor Arias's quiet presence at the courthouse doors is a living picture of this verse — faith made visible not in grand gestures but in simply showing up for the frightened. As debates rage over what a 'Christian America' should look like, this verse reminds us that Christ measured faithfulness by how we treat the stranger among us.

articles.headline: Celtic & Rangers to play Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors after fan disorder
articles.summary: According to BBC Sport, Celtic and Rangers have been ordered to play their next home Scottish Cup fixtures without spectators following incidents of fan disorder during last season's competition. The decision reflects governing bodies' response to crowd behavior issues at recent matches involving the two clubs.

articles.headline: England get early breakthrough as Archer removes Masood
articles.summary: BBC Sport reports that England made an early breakthrough on day two of the second Test at Lord's, with bowler Jofra Archer and wicketkeeper Jamie Smith combining to dismiss Pakistan captain Shan Masood for just one run. Pakistan were 5-1 in reply to England's first-innings total of 290.

verse.text: For the moment all discipline seems painful rather than pleasant, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
verse.reflection: Whether it's a club facing consequences for its fans' conduct or a bowler pressing through the early overs of a long match, sport reminds us that discipline and perseverance—though hard in the moment—often shape something better down the road.

articles.headline: Matt Lucas and Hugh Bonneville among actors calling for law on AI voice cloning
articles.summary: According to BBC News, actors Matt Lucas and Hugh Bonneville are among performers calling on the UK government to introduce a legal right for every person to own their own voice. The push comes amid growing concerns in the entertainment industry over AI voice cloning technology being used without consent.

articles.headline: What we know after the big Grand Theft Auto 6 preview
articles.summary: BBC News reports that an official preview of the highly anticipated video game Grand Theft Auto 6 has been released, drawing strong reactions from fans and critics. The outlet describes the response to the preview as largely positive.

verse.text: For you created my inmost being; you knit me together in my mother's womb. I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made.
verse.reflection: As technology makes it possible to imitate even a person's voice, it's worth remembering that each of us was intentionally and uniquely made by God, not manufactured or replicated. May today's conversations about AI and identity remind us to honor the individuality God has woven into every person.

closingBlessing: Whatever today holds, go into it steady — you've already been reminded who's holding it. — Numbers 6:24-26
